title: Review of c42's slow-fuel standing ecology on fresh seed 5: segregated prey and worm-like predator patches persist to t=12000 (8 predator components at the end); prey divide more than in the predator-free twin (8 vs 4 persistent splits, generation 2 vs 1), a smaller gap than on c42's seeds
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py with WORLD_P {"Du":0.3} at 128^2 on new seed 5 (labkit, 120 frames to t=12000; rerun/seed5) and its matched predator-free twin ({"Du":0.3,"pred_on":0}, same seed; rerun/seed5_twin_nopred). Sheet: from the noisy start, prey droplets and worm-like predator condensates form by t~500. The predators gather into slowly shifting patches, which hold from t~3000 to 12000, while the rest of the box is a field of prey droplets; there are no box-wide cycles. labkit: predators 8 components at the end (mean 17.8, max 34), 0 persistent splits, merge/split 1.69; prey 38 components at the end, 8 persistent splits, max generation 2, merge/split 0.11. Predator-free twin: 103 static prey droplets, 4 persistent splits, max generation 1. So predators persist and prey turn over more with them than without them, as c42 reports, but my prey-split gap (8 vs 4) is smaller than c42's seed 0 (14 vs 0).

observations.X: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=3000-12000: segregated predator patches beside a prey droplet field, predators alive at t=12000 (FACTS: 8 predator components); prey persistent splits 8 (generation 2) vs 4 (generation 1) in rerun/seed5_twin_nopred, which ends as 103 static prey droplets

seeds_run.result: pass (predators persist; prey splits 8 vs 4 in the twin)

controls_run.X: rerun/seed5_twin_nopred (pred_on 0, same seed, grid and duration)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at 128^2. The prey-split excess over the twin is 2x here (8 vs 4), against 14 vs 0, 8 vs 5 and 3 vs 1 on c42's seeds, so the size of the effect varies a lot between seeds. Predators do not reproduce (0 persistent splits).
